Action Plan:
1. Suspected left olecranon bursitis – commence ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; stop if heartburn occurs.
2. Arrange venous blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatology antibodies, serum urate) – laboratory request form to be posted to patient.
3. Patient to attend phlebotomy as soon as form received; results expected ~5–6 days after sampling.
4. Schedule follow-up consultation (video or face-to-face per patient preference) once results available to review findings and reassess elbow.
5. Safety-netting: if elbow becomes markedly red, increasingly painful, or erythema spreads, patient to seek urgent medical review for possible septic arthritis.
6. Lifestyle: continue normal activity; no need for work restriction at present.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: painless swelling over left elbow noticed ~1 week ago. Mild warmth, slight tenderness adjacent to tip; no trauma history.  
• Review of systems: denies systemic symptoms; normal elbow range of motion.  
• Past medical history: osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP several years ago).  
• Allergies: peanuts. No known drug allergies.  
• Medications: none routinely.  
• Social history: desk-based job; runs 2–3×/week; otherwise fit and active.

Objective:
• Video inspection: visible soft swelling over left olecranon area; skin slightly dry; no obvious erythema; full active movement preserved.  
• Palpation (patient-assisted): area slightly warmer than surrounding skin; minimal focal tenderness lateral to olecranon; no marked pain at olecranon tip.  
• No vitals provided.  
• No investigations yet performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling  
   - Assessment: Probable olecranon bursitis.  
   - Differential: septic bursitis/arthritis, gouty tophus, rheumatoid nodule.  
   - Investigations: ESR/CRP, FBC, rheumatoid factor/anti-CCP, serum urate.  
   - Treatment: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; patient education on NSAID precautions.  
   - Referral: consider in-person GP or MSK clinic review if deterioration or abnormal blood results.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing clinically expected elements: vital signs, full drug/allergy reconciliation beyond peanuts.  
• Internal conflicts: none noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; minimal background noise.
